current.text: He signed a minimum contract to return to Orlando as a backup.
Orlando's projected starting center is Wendell Carter Jr. Vucevic is projected on the bench as the backup center. Goga Bitadze will still get some minutes.
Experts expect a reserve role of about 15 to 22 minutes, down from 28 last season. He could even end up third string.
Last season's numbers overrate him. His finish came from starting in Chicago, and his two-point scoring fell off a cliff in Boston, where he looked washed.
He is a late swing pick around rounds 12 to 13. If he gets 23 to 25 minutes, he beats that draft spot.
Drafting him at a starter's price in the top 80 to 90 is a mistake.
He has more upside if Wendell Carter Jr. gets hurt. In that case he could be top 100.
Orlando added him to fix its bench scoring, which ranked 27th or 28th last season. He can still score 12 to 14 points a game off the bench.
Some luck helped his assists. He converted 68% of potential assists.
Sean Sweeney is Orlando's new head coach, so rotation roles may change.

durable.text: He shoots threes at decent volume for a big and is a good rebounder.
He gets rebounds without blocks, and he never gets steals. Steals are his weakest category for a center.
He is a pretty good passer for a big man.

note: Our league paid 17 USD for him last season. The market has dropped to about 1 USD (Yahoo 1.0, ESPN 1.3) now that he is Wendell Carter Jr.'s backup. Treat him as a 1 USD end-of-draft flyer and a Carter handcuff, not a starter: projections of 8.6 to 13.8 points depend on whether he gets about 25 minutes. He fits punt STL builds that want rebounds and some threes from a center. Early in the season, check his minutes against Carter and Bitadze under new coach Sweeney, and drop him fast if he stays near 15 to 20 minutes.
